title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering
excerpt: AI makes projects with weak engineering culture fail much faster.
content_html:
It's 2020. You're the most senior person on your team, in charge of code quality and architecture. You've set up good engineering practices, you thoroughly review PRs from people who are less experienced than you and work hard to maintain a healthy codebase.

Then at some point, you go on holiday. When you come back, the codebase is a mess. Everyone merged each other's PRs without really paying much attention, someone added a bunch of new tables to the database to denormalise it because it was easier and they added serverless or Kafka to the stack without any solid evidence that they needed either.

It's okay. You can fix this.

Fast forward to 2026. You haven't been on holiday. It's just a normal Monday morning. You make yourself a nice coffee, open your computer and find yourself with 7 PRs to review. You open the first one: +24506 -3938 lines, accompanied by some AI-generated description of what they're supposed to do. Somehow, your team has made more changes since Friday than they used to make while you were away for a few weeks.

AI removed the speed limit

AI makes projects with weak engineering culture fail much faster.

There used to be a time when people sat down and talked about how they'd do something. Now they can just prompt an agent for a few hours and open a PR.

The most tragic aspect of this way of working is that, to the untrained eye, it works.

If you pull the branch and test it, you'll probably get something somewhat functional. So what do they do? They keep going. Again and again. Until the project reaches a point where no one knows how anything works.

Just like someone buying a new luxury car on a credit card. You don't see the debt. You just see the car that looks great.

But then users start to report a weird bug. It's the 4th time your team has been trying to fix it. I mean... asking AI to fix it. Unfortunately, it seems like not even Fable can figure it out.

You go talk to the person who worked on this feature.

  • "So where does the data come from?"
  • "Hmm... actually I don't know. Let me ask Claude."

You sit next to each other watching an endless wall of text appear on the screen. Neither of you has any idea whether any of it is true but Claude seems very confident.

"Let's just turn on ultracode and ask it to double-check?"

This one will take a while. You start talking about the latest drama on X.

You finally get an answer back.

  • "Does this make any sense to you?"
  • "I'm not sure."
  • "Didn't you build this like... last week?"

Silence.

This project has become so convoluted, with so many layers and services, that no one on your team could possibly start to understand what's going on.

So, what do you do?

Fixing it would require such a colossal amount of work that it would be impossible to even start justifying it to anyone in management.

And what are you even thinking about? It would end up in the exact same state again in just a few months anyway.

  • "Let's just ask Claude to fix it."
  • "Okay. I'll create a loop and goal so it doesn't stop until it's checked that everything works."
  • "Sounds good"
  • "Actually, I ran out of Fable usage for today so I'll run it tomorrow"

You grab another coffee and walk back to your computer. You now have 13 PRs left to review. You see something you don't quite understand, so you message the person who wrote it.

  • "Why are we doing this here?"

They send you a link. It's a Claude conversation.

Somewhere in that conversation, buried between Claude confidently recommending one architecture, apologising, changing its mind, your coworker asking it to reconsider again and another 15 rounds of changes, is apparently the design decision behind this code.

  • "Which part should I read?"
  • "Probably all of it."

Does this sound familiar?

Whenever I talk about this, someone eventually tells me that nobody ever fully understood large systems anyway. It's true.

You were never expected to understand every service and every database. But at least someone did and would explain it to you.

Now they ask an LLM because they don't actually know themselves.

You can't afford bad engineers anymore

In every team, there are competent people who make the project possible. There are also people who essentially make it harder for everyone else. And now anyone can produce more code in a day than they used to in a year.

In the story above, everyone is failing:

  • The engineer opening a 25,000-line PR should have stopped the agent long before it got there. They should have understood what it was doing, broken the work into smaller pieces and questioned every new abstraction it introduced.
  • The person reviewing it should have refused to review something that large instead of giving in.
  • The person adding Kafka should have been able to explain exactly why it was needed.
  • The person who built the feature should have been able to explain where the data came from without sending a link to a Claude conversation.

But what's the problem then? Just use AI to fix it. Well, it's not that easy...

Before anyone jumps on this, none of this means technical debt is always bad. The important part is that you know it's a shortcut.

Anyway, reverting a bad decision is hard. Very hard.

For example, how long would it take an LLM to add a bunch of tables and columns to the database? 10 minutes?

But once you start storing data there, you can't just remove them. You have to come up with a migration plan, make sure you don't disrupt the system because people are paying to use this every day. You have to think about what you'll do if the migration fails. Make sure you don't end up with orphaned foreign keys. It's just so much harder to fix. Even with the best model you can get.

And while you're fixing it, more PRs keep coming in. More code, more abstractions, more decisions. A person can generate 20,000 lines of code in an afternoon, but you still have to sit there and understand what those lines actually do.

By the time you've untangled one bad decision, five more have been merged.

The new AI economy

Of course, bad engineers were always a liability.

It has been like this for decades, well before OpenAI or Anthropic existed. Bad decisions compounded, unnecessary complexity accumulated and teams ended up maintaining systems nobody really understood.

The difference is that there used to be a limit to how fast you could do it.

Today, implementation is cheap. You are paid to make good decisions. To build software that will scale while managing complexity.

Ask yourself why companies are paying six-figure salaries for engineers in London or San Francisco in the first place.

If all they needed was someone who could turn a specification into working code, why were they paying that much when they could already get it done cheaply elsewhere?

Why are the tech companies claiming that "software is solved" still paying top salaries to attract the best people they can?

My bet is that AI pushes salaries further apart. To be employable, there's a bar you have to clear and that bar is whatever the current best model du jour can do.

Good engineers have become more valuable because AI lets them move much faster. They don't need as many people around them just to do the implementation work anymore.

At the same time, bad engineers have become much more expensive to hire.

I wrote about this before when I said the vibe coder career path is doomed.

You need to contribute beyond what everyone already gets by giving an agent a prompt.

If you lack the judgment required to evaluate the LLM's recommendation, asking for more judgment doesn't solve the problem.

At some point, someone still has to know what is going on. And that's the most valuable person on the team.

The people who don't will become much cheaper to hire or get replaced entirely while the money gets funnelled towards an increasingly smaller number of people who can actually be trusted.

I don't think this is going to be limited to software engineering either. I believe the same thing is going to happen across most knowledge work. AI will make the best people much more productive and the bad ones almost impossible to hire. Before, there was a good chance someone would catch their bad decisions before they went too far. Now they can make changes faster than anyone around them can realistically review or understand them.

Answers to the most common objections

"Bad engineers always existed"

The difference is the speed.

It is the difference between crashing at 30 km/h and crashing at 200 km/h. Before AI, a bad engineer would struggle to produce code that even compiled. When they did produce something, it took them a long time and the blast radius was limited. The damage was bounded by how fast a human could type.

Now a bad engineer can produce 10,000 lines of working code before lunch. The damage we can do in an afternoon used to take them months. The speed at which bad decisions compound has changed completely while the speed at which you can fix them has not.

"Just fix your process"

Several people argued that the real problem is lack of process. If you had proper tests, CI, code review and architectural reviews, AI-generated slop wouldn't get through.

We had all of those things. None of them disappeared.

The problem is that they were designed for a world where producing a massive amount of change was impossible. Code review don't work anymore when someone opens 10 PRs a day with an AI-generated description. Tests work when they cover the behaviours you thought to test. They do not catch the behaviours nobody thought to test.

How many times have you had a completely green CI with full coverage and still shipped a bug?

The difficulty of producing code was by itself one of the limiting factors.

If the people trying to understand changes and guard quality are now the bottleneck, you have three options. Generate less, find a genuinely better way to validate or accept lower quality.

"You are just anti-AI"

Everytime I critisise AI someone says I'm a Luddism. I'm refusing to adapt to the new world, clinging to the old ways.

I use AI heavily. I have said this repeatedly. I use it every day and I have no interest in going back to writing everything by hand.

The point is that we have made producing large changes extremely cheap and fast while understanding those changes is still slow, difficult work. We have no shortcut for building a correct mental model of what a change does.

Maybe one day we will find one. As of today, I do not think we have one.

You can be a heavy AI user and still recognise that there are serious problems with how it is being used.

"More output means more productive"

Someone generates 10 PRs in a day, the numbers look incredible, surely this person is ten times more productive.

Not necessarily. The supposed 10x engineer may simply be someone stealing productivity from everyone around them.

If I generate 10 PRs in a day but three engineers now have to spend the next two days reviewing them, figuring out what I changed, correcting bad assumptions, debugging regressions and explaining why half of it needs to be redone, I have not become 10x more productive. I have just moved the work onto other people.

Worse, I am consuming the time of the people who are usually the hardest to replace and whose attention is already scarce.

PR count, lines changed and features "completed" are terrible measures of productivity. You can make your own numbers look incredible while reducing the throughput of the entire team.

Some people pushed back on this by saying the real problem is bad organisations with broken incentives. It's true. If your company rewards ticket count over quality, the careful engineer looks like the bad employee and the sloppy one gets promoted.

"Pushing back just makes you're the toxic one"

Someone pointed out that trying to hold the line on quality can get you labelled as toxic. Everyone else is shipping fast and you are the person saying "wait".

I would much rather have someone on my team who ships less but whose work I can trust than someone much faster whose changes leave me wondering what problems we're going to discover later.

You need to be flexible and compromise when the business trade-off makes sense. But you also need a backbone. If you think something is going to cause real problems, bringing it up is part of the job.

And when production breaks, and it will, I need the person who made the change to actually understand it well enough to help fix it. Not show up with no idea what is going on.

"Just AI output is like assembly from a compiler"

We already trust compilers to produce machine code we do not read. Why is this different?

A compiler takes code and translates it into another representation while preserving its semantics. The compiler is not deciding what your system should do. It is deterministic.

An LLM is making decisions. It is choosing architectures, picking abstractions, deciding where to put things. When you ask Claude to build a feature, it is not translating your intent into code. It is making dozens of design decisions on your behalf.

If in five years I can give an agent a complete specification and reliably verify the resulting code against it, then sure, reviewing code may become obsolete and I would happily stop doing it. We are not there yet.

If you genuinely understand the resulting system, that is fine. That is not the behaviour I am criticising. But for the vast majority of very large PRs, especially AI-generated ones, I would bet money that the person opening it does not actually understand all of it.

"We ship 99% AI-generated code and it works"

I do the same. Most of the code I produce comes from AI.

You still have to put in the work to understand the result. If you are shipping AI code and you genuinely understand the system, you are doing it right. The article is not about you.

"AI can write the code" ≠ "I do not need to understand it anymore."

You can use AI heavily and still take responsibility for what it produces.

"Users don't care. It's just a CRUD app. Ship it and get paid"

I tend to find that this perspective comes from people working on relatively small or isolated projects.

On a large system, the customer being happy today is not enough. You need other engineers to be able to understand the system. Have you ever been on call and been woken up in the middle of the night to fix a production incident in a system you did not write?

If everything you build is small, isolated and easy to replace, then sure. Ship the ugly thing, get paid and move on. If you are going to be working on something for the next five years or more, you should probably spend some time thinking about what you are doing.

Nobody is getting paid significant money just to build a simple CRUD app. Even before AI. Companies pay experienced engineers because the supposedly simple CRUD sits inside a messy real system with years of business rules, constraints and integrations where bad decisions have consequences.

"What about junior developers?"

I have worked with two junior developers recently who are very good precisely because they are trying to understand what they are doing rather than just producing code. They use AI to explore things they do not understand, ask questions to clarify their reasoning and double-check assumptions. They use the tools to increase their understanding.

I have also worked with senior developers who basically gave up and stopped trying to understand the code. They became much worse engineers as a result. At this point I would much rather work with those two juniors.

The problem is not AI. The problem is using AI as a substitute for understanding instead of a tool for building it.

Related to this, some people argued that we should not teach skills that AI can do better. The fact that a machine can do something better than humans does not automatically make learning it pointless.

We still teach arithmetic and algebra despite computers being vastly better at calculation. We teach spelling, grammar and essay writing. We even teach history and geography while everyone permanently has a device in their pocket that can look up almost any fact in seconds.

How else would you be developing the mental models required to understand, question and verify anything?

"Using AI is just delegation, like a manager"

A manager is not normally the person deciding how the software should be architected or implemented. Their job is largely priorities, people, coordination and resource allocation.

You are still an engineer. But you have delegated your technical judgement to an LLM. You just stopped doing the most important part of your job.

"Not all technical debt is bad"

Agreed. Debt is debt. Some of it is absolutely worth taking on.

I do not have any issue with intentional debt when you understand the trade-off and have a clear payoff plan.

"How do we make more senior devs if we don't hire juniors anymore?"

By reducing the number of entry-level engineering roles, the industry is sabotaging its own future. Fewer people learning means fewer people capable of maintaining systems down the line.

It's true. But the industry does not really owe people opportunities. Even if you think it should, that is not how companies are going to behave.

That said, maintenance is the essence of the software industry. LLMs cannot modify projects spanning hundreds of thousands of lines. The skill required to partition architectures is still entirely human. Learn that.

They will care when nothing works, nobody seems able to fix it, building new features takes forever and every change breaks something somewhere else.

blocks.html_en: At the same time, bad engineers have become much more expensive to hire.

sentences.en: At the same time, bad engineers have become much more expensive to hire.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，雇佣糟糕的工程师的成本也变得更高。

blocks.html_en: I wrote about this before when I said the vibe coder career path is doomed.

sentences.en: I wrote about this before when I said the vibe coder career path is doomed.
sentences.zh: 我之前写过这一点，当时我说氛围程序员的职业道路是注定的。

blocks.html_en: You need to contribute beyond what everyone already gets by giving an agent a prompt.

sentences.en: You need to contribute beyond what everyone already gets by giving an agent a prompt.
sentences.zh: 您需要通过向代理提供提示来做出超出每个人已经获得的贡献。

blocks.html_en: If you lack the judgment required to evaluate the LLM's recommendation, asking for more judgment doesn't solve the problem.

sentences.en: If you lack the judgment required to evaluate the LLM's recommendation, asking for more judgment doesn't solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果您缺乏评估法学硕士推荐所需的判断力，要求更多判断力并不能解决问题。

blocks.html_en: At some point, someone still has to know what is going on. And that's the most valuable person on the team.

sentences.en: At some point, someone still has to know what is going on.
sentences.zh: 在某些时候，仍然需要有人知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And that's the most valuable person on the team.
sentences.zh: 这是团队中最有价值的人。

blocks.html_en: The people who don't will become much cheaper to hire or get replaced entirely while the money gets funnelled towards an increasingly smaller number of people who can actually be trusted.

sentences.en: The people who don't will become much cheaper to hire or get replaced entirely while the money gets funnelled towards an increasingly smaller number of people who can actually be trusted.
sentences.zh: 那些不这样做的人的雇佣成本会大大降低，或者被完全取代，而资金会流向越来越少的真正值得信任的人。

blocks.html_en: I don't think this is going to be limited to software engineering either. I believe the same thing is going to happen across most knowledge work. AI will make the best people much more productive and the bad ones almost impossible to hire. Before, there was a good chance someone would catch their bad decisions before they went too far. Now they can make changes faster than anyone around them can realistically review or understand them.

sentences.en: I don't think this is going to be limited to software engineering either.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也不会仅限于软件工程。

sentences.en: I believe the same thing is going to happen across most knowledge work.
sentences.zh: 我相信大多数知识工作都会发生同样的事情。

sentences.en: AI will make the best people much more productive and the bad ones almost impossible to hire.
sentences.zh: 人工智能将使最优秀的人变得更有生产力，而最差的人几乎不可能被雇用。

sentences.en: Before, there was a good chance someone would catch their bad decisions before they went too far.
sentences.zh: 以前，很有可能有人会在做出错误决定之前发现他们的错误。

sentences.en: Now they can make changes faster than anyone around them can realistically review or understand them.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们做出改变的速度比周围任何人能够实际审查或理解它们的速度都要快。

blocks.html_en: Answers to the most common objections

sentences.en: Answers to the most common objections
sentences.zh: 对最常见反对意见的回答

blocks.html_en: The difference is the speed.

sentences.en: The difference is the speed.
sentences.zh: 区别在于速度。

blocks.html_en: It is the difference between crashing at 30 km/h and crashing at 200 km/h. Before AI, a bad engineer would struggle to produce code that even compiled. When they did produce something, it took them a long time and the blast radius was limited. The damage was bounded by how fast a human could type.

sentences.en: It is the difference between crashing at 30 km/h and crashing at 200 km/h.
sentences.zh: 这是时速 30 公里和时速 200 公里碰撞之间的区别。

sentences.en: Before AI, a bad engineer would struggle to produce code that even compiled.
sentences.zh: 在人工智能出现之前，一个糟糕的工程师甚至很难编写出可以编译的代码。

sentences.en: When they did produce something, it took them a long time and the blast radius was limited.
sentences.zh: 当他们真正生产出东西时，他们花了很长时间，而且爆炸半径也很有限。

sentences.en: The damage was bounded by how fast a human could type.
sentences.zh: 损害程度取决于人类打字的速度。

blocks.html_en: Now a bad engineer can produce 10,000 lines of working code before lunch. The damage we can do in an afternoon used to take them months. The speed at which bad decisions compound has changed completely while the speed at which you can fix them has not.

sentences.en: Now a bad engineer can produce 10,000 lines of working code before lunch.
sentences.zh: 现在，一个糟糕的工程师可以在午饭前写出 10,000 行工作代码。

sentences.en: The damage we can do in an afternoon used to take them months.
sentences.zh: 我们一个下午所能造成的损害，过去却要花费他们几个月的时间。

sentences.en: The speed at which bad decisions compound has changed completely while the speed at which you can fix them has not.
sentences.zh: 错误决策复合的速度已经完全改变，而修复它们的速度却没有改变。

blocks.html_en: Several people argued that the real problem is lack of process. If you had proper tests, CI, code review and architectural reviews, AI-generated slop wouldn't get through.

sentences.en: Several people argued that the real problem is lack of process.
sentences.zh: 一些人认为真正的问题是缺乏流程。

sentences.en: If you had proper tests, CI, code review and architectural reviews, AI-generated slop wouldn't get through.
sentences.zh: 如果你有适当的测试、CI、代码审查和架构审查，人工智能生成的溢出就不会通过。

blocks.html_en: We had all of those things. None of them disappeared.

sentences.en: We had all of those things.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有所有这些东西。

sentences.en: None of them disappeared.
sentences.zh: 他们都没有消失。

blocks.html_en: The problem is that they were designed for a world where producing a massive amount of change was impossible. Code review don't work anymore when someone opens 10 PRs a day with an AI-generated description. Tests work when they cover the behaviours you thought to test. They do not catch the behaviours nobody thought to test.

sentences.en: The problem is that they were designed for a world where producing a massive amount of change was impossible.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，它们是为一个不可能产生大量变革的世界而设计的。

sentences.en: Code review don't work anymore when someone opens 10 PRs a day with an AI-generated description.
sentences.zh: 当有人每天打开 10 个带有 AI 生成的描述的 PR 时，代码审查就不再起作用了。

sentences.en: Tests work when they cover the behaviours you thought to test.
sentences.zh: 当测试涵盖了您想要测试的行为时，测试就有效。

sentences.en: They do not catch the behaviours nobody thought to test.
sentences.zh: 他们没有捕捉到没有人想要测试的行为。

blocks.html_en: How many times have you had a completely green CI with full coverage and still shipped a bug?

sentences.en: How many times have you had a completely green CI with full coverage and still shipped a bug?
sentences.zh: 有多少次您拥有完全覆盖的完全绿色 CI，但仍然出现错误？

blocks.html_en: The difficulty of producing code was by itself one of the limiting factors.

sentences.en: The difficulty of producing code was by itself one of the limiting factors.
sentences.zh: 生成代码的难度本身就是限制因素之一。

blocks.html_en: If the people trying to understand changes and guard quality are now the bottleneck, you have three options. Generate less, find a genuinely better way to validate or accept lower quality.

sentences.en: If the people trying to understand changes and guard quality are now the bottleneck, you have three options.
sentences.zh: 如果试图理解变化和保护质量的人现在成为瓶颈，那么你有三个选择。

sentences.en: Generate less, find a genuinely better way to validate or accept lower quality.
sentences.zh: 减少生成，找到真正更好的方法来验证或接受较低的质量。

blocks.html_en: Everytime I critisise AI someone says I'm a Luddism. I'm refusing to adapt to the new world, clinging to the old ways.

sentences.en: Everytime I critisise AI someone says I'm a Luddism.
sentences.zh: 每当我批评人工智能时，就会有人说我是卢德主义。

sentences.en: I'm refusing to adapt to the new world, clinging to the old ways.
sentences.zh: 我拒绝适应新世界，坚持旧的方式。

blocks.html_en: I use AI heavily. I have said this repeatedly. I use it every day and I have no interest in going back to writing everything by hand.

sentences.en: I use AI heavily.
sentences.zh: 我大量使用人工智能。

sentences.en: I have said this repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 这一点我已经说过很多次了。

sentences.en: I use it every day and I have no interest in going back to writing everything by hand.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用它，而且我没有兴趣回去手写所有内容。

blocks.html_en: The point is that we have made producing large changes extremely cheap and fast while understanding those changes is still slow, difficult work. We have no shortcut for building a correct mental model of what a change does.

sentences.en: The point is that we have made producing large changes extremely cheap and fast while understanding those changes is still slow, difficult work.
sentences.zh: 关键是，我们已经使大规模变更变得极其便宜和快速，而理解这些变更仍然是一项缓慢而困难的工作。

sentences.en: We have no shortcut for building a correct mental model of what a change does.
sentences.zh: 对于变革的作用，我们没有建立正确的心理模型的捷径。

blocks.html_en: Maybe one day we will find one. As of today, I do not think we have one.

sentences.en: Maybe one day we will find one.
sentences.zh: 也许有一天我们会找到一个。

sentences.en: As of today, I do not think we have one.
sentences.zh: 截至今天，我认为我们还没有。

blocks.html_en: You can be a heavy AI user and still recognise that there are serious problems with how it is being used.

sentences.en: You can be a heavy AI user and still recognise that there are serious problems with how it is being used.
sentences.zh: 你可能是人工智能的重度用户，但仍然认识到它的使用方式存在严重问题。

blocks.html_en: Someone generates 10 PRs in a day, the numbers look incredible, surely this person is ten times more productive.

sentences.en: Someone generates 10 PRs in a day, the numbers look incredible, surely this person is ten times more productive.
sentences.zh: 有人一天产生 10 个 PR，这个数字看起来令人难以置信，这个人的生产力肯定是原来的十倍。

blocks.html_en: Not necessarily. The supposed 10x engineer may simply be someone stealing productivity from everyone around them.

sentences.en: Not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 未必。

sentences.en: The supposed 10x engineer may simply be someone stealing productivity from everyone around them.
sentences.zh: 所谓的 10 倍工程师可能只是窃取周围每个人生产力的人。

blocks.html_en: If I generate 10 PRs in a day but three engineers now have to spend the next two days reviewing them, figuring out what I changed, correcting bad assumptions, debugging regressions and explaining why half of it needs to be redone, I have not become 10x more productive. I have just moved the work onto other people.

sentences.en: If I generate 10 PRs in a day but three engineers now have to spend the next two days reviewing them, figuring out what I changed, correcting bad assumptions, debugging regressions and explaining why half of it needs to be redone, I have not become 10x more productive.
sentences.zh: 如果我一天生成 10 个 PR，但现在三位工程师必须在接下来的两天内审查它们，找出我更改的内容，纠正错误的假设，调试回归并解释为什么需要重做一半，那么我的工作效率并没有提高 10 倍。

sentences.en: I have just moved the work onto other people.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚把工作移交给了其他人。

blocks.html_en: Worse, I am consuming the time of the people who are usually the hardest to replace and whose attention is already scarce.

sentences.en: Worse, I am consuming the time of the people who are usually the hardest to replace and whose attention is already scarce.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，我正在消耗那些通常最难被取代且注意力已经稀缺的人的时间。

blocks.html_en: PR count, lines changed and features "completed" are terrible measures of productivity. You can make your own numbers look incredible while reducing the throughput of the entire team.

sentences.en: PR count, lines changed and features "completed" are terrible measures of productivity.
sentences.zh: PR 数量、更改的行数和“完成”的功能都是糟糕的生产力衡量标准。

sentences.en: You can make your own numbers look incredible while reducing the throughput of the entire team.
sentences.zh: 您可以让自己的数字看起来令人难以置信，同时降低整个团队的吞吐量。

blocks.html_en: Some people pushed back on this by saying the real problem is bad organisations with broken incentives. It's true. If your company rewards ticket count over quality, the careful engineer looks like the bad employee and the sloppy one gets promoted.

sentences.en: Some people pushed back on this by saying the real problem is bad organisations with broken incentives.
sentences.zh: 有些人反驳说，真正的问题是缺乏激励机制的不良组织。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 这是真的。

sentences.en: If your company rewards ticket count over quality, the careful engineer looks like the bad employee and the sloppy one gets promoted.
sentences.zh: 如果你的公司重视票数而不是质量，那么细心的工程师看起来就像是坏员工，而马虎的工程师就会得到晋升。

blocks.html_en: Someone pointed out that trying to hold the line on quality can get you labelled as toxic. Everyone else is shipping fast and you are the person saying "wait".

sentences.en: Someone pointed out that trying to hold the line on quality can get you labelled as toxic.
sentences.zh: 有人指出，试图控制质量可能会让你被贴上有毒的标签。

sentences.en: Everyone else is shipping fast and you are the person saying "wait".
sentences.zh: 其他人都在快速发货，而你是那个说“等等”的人。

blocks.html_en: I would much rather have someone on my team who ships less but whose work I can trust than someone much faster whose changes leave me wondering what problems we're going to discover later.

sentences.en: I would much rather have someone on my team who ships less but whose work I can trust than someone much faster whose changes leave me wondering what problems we're going to discover later.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿我的团队中有一个发货量较少但其工作我可以信任的人，而不是一个速度更快的人，他的变化让我想知道我们稍后会发现什么问题。

blocks.html_en: You need to be flexible and compromise when the business trade-off makes sense. But you also need a backbone. If you think something is going to cause real problems, bringing it up is part of the job.

sentences.en: You need to be flexible and compromise when the business trade-off makes sense.
sentences.zh: 当业务权衡有意义时，您需要保持灵活性和妥协。

sentences.en: But you also need a backbone.
sentences.zh: 但你还需要一个脊梁。

sentences.en: If you think something is going to cause real problems, bringing it up is part of the job.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为某件事会造成真正的问题，提出来就是工作的一部分。

blocks.html_en: And when production breaks, and it will, I need the person who made the change to actually understand it well enough to help fix it. Not show up with no idea what is going on.

sentences.en: And when production breaks, and it will, I need the person who made the change to actually understand it well enough to help fix it.
sentences.zh: 当生产中断时（确实会发生），我需要进行更改的人真正充分理解它以帮助修复它。

sentences.en: Not show up with no idea what is going on.
sentences.zh: 不出现不知道发生了什么。

blocks.html_en: We already trust compilers to produce machine code we do not read. Why is this different?

sentences.en: We already trust compilers to produce machine code we do not read.
sentences.zh: 我们已经相信编译器会生成我们不阅读的机器代码。

sentences.en: Why is this different?
sentences.zh: 为什么这不同呢？

blocks.html_en: A compiler takes code and translates it into another representation while preserving its semantics. The compiler is not deciding what your system should do. It is deterministic.

sentences.en: A compiler takes code and translates it into another representation while preserving its semantics.
sentences.zh: 编译器获取代码并将其转换为另一种表示形式，同时保留其语义。

sentences.en: The compiler is not deciding what your system should do.
sentences.zh: 编译器不会决定您的系统应该做什么。

sentences.en: It is deterministic.
sentences.zh: 它是确定性的。

blocks.html_en: An LLM is making decisions. It is choosing architectures, picking abstractions, deciding where to put things. When you ask Claude to build a feature, it is not translating your intent into code. It is making dozens of design decisions on your behalf.

sentences.en: An LLM is making decisions.
sentences.zh: 法学硕士正在做决定。

sentences.en: It is choosing architectures, picking abstractions, deciding where to put things.
sentences.zh: 它正在选择架构、选择抽象、决定把东西放在哪里。

sentences.en: When you ask Claude to build a feature, it is not translating your intent into code.
sentences.zh: 当你要求 Claude 构建一个功能时，它并没有将你的意图转化为代码。

sentences.en: It is making dozens of design decisions on your behalf.
sentences.zh: 它正在代表您做出数十个设计决策。

blocks.html_en: If in five years I can give an agent a complete specification and reliably verify the resulting code against it, then sure, reviewing code may become obsolete and I would happily stop doing it. We are not there yet.

sentences.en: If in five years I can give an agent a complete specification and reliably verify the resulting code against it, then sure, reviewing code may become obsolete and I would happily stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 如果五年后我可以给代理一个完整的规范并可靠地验证生成的代码，那么当然，审查代码可能会变得过时，我会很乐意停止这样做。

sentences.en: We are not there yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有到那一步。

blocks.html_en: If you genuinely understand the resulting system, that is fine. That is not the behaviour I am criticising. But for the vast majority of very large PRs, especially AI-generated ones, I would bet money that the person opening it does not actually understand all of it.

sentences.en: If you genuinely understand the resulting system, that is fine.
sentences.zh: 如果您真正理解最终的系统，那就没问题了。

sentences.en: That is not the behaviour I am criticising.
sentences.zh: 这不是我批评的行为。

sentences.en: But for the vast majority of very large PRs, especially AI-generated ones, I would bet money that the person opening it does not actually understand all of it.
sentences.zh: 但对于绝大多数非常大的 PR，尤其是人工智能生成的 PR，我敢打赌，打开它的人实际上并不理解所有内容。

blocks.html_en: I do the same. Most of the code I produce comes from AI.

sentences.en: I do the same.
sentences.zh: 我也这样做。

sentences.en: Most of the code I produce comes from AI.
sentences.zh: 我编写的大部分代码都来自人工智能。

blocks.html_en: You still have to put in the work to understand the result. If you are shipping AI code and you genuinely understand the system, you are doing it right. The article is not about you.

sentences.en: You still have to put in the work to understand the result.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要付出努力才能理解结果。

sentences.en: If you are shipping AI code and you genuinely understand the system, you are doing it right.
sentences.zh: 如果您正在交付人工智能代码并且您真正了解该系统，那么您就做得对。

sentences.en: The article is not about you.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章不是关于你的。

blocks.html_en: "AI can write the code" ≠ "I do not need to understand it anymore."

sentences.en: "AI can write the code" ≠ "I do not need to understand it anymore."
sentences.zh: “人工智能可以写代码”≠“我不需要再理解它了”。

blocks.html_en: You can use AI heavily and still take responsibility for what it produces.

sentences.en: You can use AI heavily and still take responsibility for what it produces.
sentences.zh: 你可以大量使用人工智能，但仍然对其产生的结果负责。

blocks.html_en: I tend to find that this perspective comes from people working on relatively small or isolated projects.

sentences.en: I tend to find that this perspective comes from people working on relatively small or isolated projects.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于发现这种观点来自于从事相对较小或孤立项目的人们。

blocks.html_en: On a large system, the customer being happy today is not enough. You need other engineers to be able to understand the system. Have you ever been on call and been woken up in the middle of the night to fix a production incident in a system you did not write?

sentences.en: On a large system, the customer being happy today is not enough.
sentences.zh: 在大型系统中，仅仅让客户满意是不够的。

sentences.en: You need other engineers to be able to understand the system.
sentences.zh: 您需要其他工程师才能理解该系统。

sentences.en: Have you ever been on call and been woken up in the middle of the night to fix a production incident in a system you did not write?
sentences.zh: 您是否曾经待命并在半夜被叫醒，以修复不是您编写的系统中的生产事件？

blocks.html_en: If everything you build is small, isolated and easy to replace, then sure. Ship the ugly thing, get paid and move on. If you are going to be working on something for the next five years or more, you should probably spend some time thinking about what you are doing.

sentences.en: If everything you build is small, isolated and easy to replace, then sure.
sentences.zh: 如果您构建的所有内容都很小、独立并且易于更换，那么当然可以。

sentences.en: Ship the ugly thing, get paid and move on.
sentences.zh: 运送丑陋的东西，获得报酬并继续前进。

sentences.en: If you are going to be working on something for the next five years or more, you should probably spend some time thinking about what you are doing.
sentences.zh: 如果你打算在未来五年或更长时间内从事某件事，你可能应该花一些时间思考你在做什么。

blocks.html_en: Nobody is getting paid significant money just to build a simple CRUD app. Even before AI. Companies pay experienced engineers because the supposedly simple CRUD sits inside a messy real system with years of business rules, constraints and integrations where bad decisions have consequences.

sentences.en: Nobody is getting paid significant money just to build a simple CRUD app.
sentences.zh: 没有人会因为构建一个简单的 CRUD 应用程序而获得大量资金。

sentences.en: Even before AI.
sentences.zh: 甚至在人工智能之前。

sentences.en: Companies pay experienced engineers because the supposedly simple CRUD sits inside a messy real system with years of business rules, constraints and integrations where bad decisions have consequences.
sentences.zh: 公司之所以向经验丰富的工程师付费，是因为看似简单的 CRUD 位于一个混乱的真实系统中，该系统具有多年的业务规则、约束和集成，而错误的决策会产生后果。

blocks.html_en: I have worked with two junior developers recently who are very good precisely because they are trying to understand what they are doing rather than just producing code. They use AI to explore things they do not understand, ask questions to clarify their reasoning and double-check assumptions. They use the tools to increase their understanding.

sentences.en: I have worked with two junior developers recently who are very good precisely because they are trying to understand what they are doing rather than just producing code.
sentences.zh: 我最近与两位初级开发人员一起工作，他们非常优秀，正是因为他们试图理解自己在做什么，而不仅仅是生成代码。

sentences.en: They use AI to explore things they do not understand, ask questions to clarify their reasoning and double-check assumptions.
sentences.zh: 他们使用人工智能来探索他们不理解的事物，提出问题以澄清他们的推理并仔细检查假设。

sentences.en: They use the tools to increase their understanding.
sentences.zh: 他们使用这些工具来增进理解。

blocks.html_en: I have also worked with senior developers who basically gave up and stopped trying to understand the code. They became much worse engineers as a result. At this point I would much rather work with those two juniors.

sentences.en: I have also worked with senior developers who basically gave up and stopped trying to understand the code.
sentences.zh: 我还与高级开发人员一起工作过，他们基本上放弃并停止尝试理解代码。

sentences.en: They became much worse engineers as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们成为了更糟糕的工程师。

sentences.en: At this point I would much rather work with those two juniors.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上我更愿意和那两个后辈一起工作。

blocks.html_en: The problem is not AI. The problem is using AI as a substitute for understanding instead of a tool for building it.

content_html_zh:
现在是 2020 年。 您是团队中最资深的人，负责代码质量和架构。 您已经建立了良好的工程实践，您彻底审查了经验不如您的人的 PR，并努力维护健康的代码库。

然后在某个时候，你去度假。 当你回来时，代码库一片混乱。 每个人都在没有真正关注的情况下合并了彼此的 PR，有人在数据库中添加了一堆新表以使其非规范化，因为它更容易，并且他们将无服务器或 Kafka 添加到堆栈中，但没有任何确凿的证据表明他们需要。

没关系。 你可以解决这个问题。

快进到 2026 年。 你还没去度假。 这只是一个普通的周一早上。 您给自己泡了一杯好咖啡，打开电脑，发现自己有 7 个 PR 需要审核。 你打开第一个：+24506 -3938 行，伴随着一些人工智能生成的关于它们应该做什么的描述。 不知何故，自周五以来，您的团队所做的更改比您离开几周时所做的更改还要多。

AI取消了速度限制

人工智能使得工程文化薄弱的项目失败得更快。

曾经有一段时间，人们坐下来讨论他们将如何做某事。 现在，他们只需提示代理几个小时即可打开 PR。

这种工作方式最悲惨的一点是，在未经训练的人看来，它确实有效。

如果你拉出分支并测试它，你可能会得到一些功能性的东西。 那么他们做什么呢？ 他们继续前进。 一次又一次。 直到项目达到无人知道任何事情如何运作的地步。

就像有人用信用卡购买一辆新的豪华车一样。 你看不到债务。 你只是看到这辆车看起来很棒。

但随后用户开始报告一个奇怪的错误。 这是您的团队第四次尝试修复该问题。 我是说... 要求人工智能修复它。 不幸的是，似乎连《神鬼寓言》都无法弄清楚。

你去和开发这个功能的人谈谈。

  • “那么数据从哪里来呢？”
  • “唔... 其实我不知道。 我去问问克劳德吧。”

你们坐在一起，看着屏幕上出现无尽的文字墙。 你们都不知道这些是否属实，但克劳德似乎很有信心。

“让我们打开超级代码并要求它进行双重检查？”

这需要一段时间。 你开始谈论 X 上的最新电视剧。

你终于得到答案了。

  • “这对你来说有意义吗？”
  • “我不知道。”
  • “你不是把这个建得像... 上星期？”

沉默。

这个项目已经变得如此复杂，有如此多的层和服务，以至于你的团队中没有人能够开始理解正在发生的事情。

那么，你做什么呢？

解决这个问题需要大量的工作，甚至不可能向管理层的任何人证明它的合理性。

你到底在想什么？ 无论如何，它最终会在短短几个月内再次处于完全相同的状态。

  • “还是请克劳德来解决吧。”
  • “好的。 我将创建一个循环和目标，以便在检查一切正常之前它不会停止。”
  • “听起来不错”
  • “事实上，我今天的《神鬼寓言》用完了，所以我明天再运行它”

你又喝了一杯咖啡，然后走回电脑前。 您现在还有 13 个 PR 需要审核。 你看到一些你不太理解的东西，所以你给写它的人发消息。

  • “我们为什么要在这里这样做？”

他们向您发送一个链接。 这是克劳德的谈话。

在那次对话中的某个地方，隐藏在 Claude 自信地推荐一种架构、道歉、改变主意、你的同事要求它重新考虑以及另外 15 轮变更之间，显然是这段代码背后的设计决策。

  • “我应该读哪一部分？”
  • “可能是全部。”

这听起来很熟悉吗？

每当我谈论这个时，最终有人告诉我，无论如何，没有人完全理解大型系统。 这是真的。

你永远不会被期望了解每一项服务和每一个数据库。 但至少有人这样做了并且会向你解释。

现在他们要求法学硕士，因为他们实际上并不了解自己。

你再也买不起糟糕的工程师了

每个团队中都有有能力的人使项目成为可能。 也有一些人本质上让其他人的处境变得更加困难。 现在，任何人在一天内生成的代码都比以前一年生成的代码还要多。

在上面的故事中，每个人都失败了：

  • 打开 25,000 行 PR 的工程师应该早在代理到达之前就将其停止。 他们应该理解它在做什么，将工作分解成更小的部分，并对它引入的每一个新抽象提出质疑。
  • 审查它的人应该拒绝审查这么大的东西，而不是屈服。
  • 添加 Kafka 的人应该能够准确解释为什么需要它。
  • 构建该功能的人应该能够解释数据的来源，而无需发送克劳德对话的链接。

但那有什么问题呢？ 只需使用 AI 来修复它即可。 嗯，这并不容易...

在任何人开始讨论这一点之前，这并不意味着技术债务总是不好的。 重要的是你知道这是一条捷径。

不管怎样，改变一个错误的决定是很困难的。 非常难。

例如，法学硕士向数据库添加一堆表和列需要多长时间？ 10分钟？

但一旦开始在那里存储数据，就不能直接删除它们。 你必须制定一个迁移计划，确保你不会破坏系统，因为人们每天都付费使用它。 您必须考虑如果迁移失败该怎么办。 确保您最终不会得到孤立的外键。 修复起来要困难得多。 即使您拥有最好的模型。

当你修复它时，更多的 PR 不断出现。 更多代码、更多抽象、更多决策。 一个人可以在一个下午生成 20,000 行代码，但你仍然必须坐在那里了解这些行实际上做了什么。

当你解决了一个错误的决定时，另外五个决定已经被合并。

人工智能新经济

当然，糟糕的工程师总是一种责任。

几十年来一直如此，早在 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 出现之前。 错误的决策变得更加复杂，不必要的复杂性不断累积，团队最终维护的系统无人真正理解。

不同之处在于，过去你的速度是有限制的。

如今，实施成本低廉。 你得到报酬是为了做出正确的决定。 构建可扩展的软件，同时管理复杂性。

首先问问自己，为什么公司要为伦敦或旧金山的工程师支付六位数的薪水。

如果他们需要的只是一个能够将规范转化为工作代码的人，那么当他们已经可以在其他地方以低廉的成本完成它时，为什么还要支付那么多费用呢？

为什么声称“软件已解决”的科技公司仍然支付高薪来吸引最优秀的人才？

我敢打赌，人工智能会让薪资差距进一步拉大。 要想找到工作，你必须突破一个门槛，而这个门槛就是当前最好的模特所能做到的。

优秀的工程师变得更有价值，因为人工智能让他们的行动速度更快。 他们不再需要周围那么多人来完成实施工作。

与此同时，雇佣糟糕的工程师的成本也变得更高。

我之前写过这一点，当时我说氛围程序员的职业道路是注定的。

您需要通过向代理提供提示来做出超出每个人已经获得的贡献。

如果您缺乏评估法学硕士推荐所需的判断力，要求更多判断力并不能解决问题。

在某些时候，仍然需要有人知道发生了什么。 这是团队中最有价值的人。

那些不这样做的人的雇佣成本会大大降低，或者被完全取代，而资金会流向越来越少的真正值得信任的人。

我认为这也不会仅限于软件工程。 我相信大多数知识工作都会发生同样的事情。 人工智能将使最优秀的人变得更有生产力，而最差的人几乎不可能被雇用。 以前，很有可能有人会在做出错误决定之前发现他们的错误。 现在，他们做出改变的速度比周围任何人能够实际审查或理解它们的速度都要快。

对最常见反对意见的回答

"Bad engineers always existed"

区别在于速度。

这是时速 30 公里和时速 200 公里碰撞之间的区别。 在人工智能出现之前，一个糟糕的工程师甚至很难编写出可以编译的代码。 当他们真正生产出东西时，他们花了很长时间，而且爆炸半径也很有限。 损害程度取决于人类打字的速度。

现在，一个糟糕的工程师可以在午饭前写出 10,000 行工作代码。 我们一个下午所能造成的损害，过去却要花费他们几个月的时间。 错误决策复合的速度已经完全改变，而修复它们的速度却没有改变。

"Just fix your process"

一些人认为真正的问题是缺乏流程。 如果你有适当的测试、CI、代码审查和架构审查，人工智能生成的溢出就不会通过。

我们拥有所有这些东西。 他们都没有消失。

问题在于，它们是为一个不可能产生大量变革的世界而设计的。 当有人每天打开 10 个带有 AI 生成的描述的 PR 时，代码审查就不再起作用了。 当测试涵盖了您想要测试的行为时，测试就有效。 他们没有捕捉到没有人想要测试的行为。

有多少次您拥有完全覆盖的完全绿色 CI，但仍然出现错误？

生成代码的难度本身就是限制因素之一。

如果试图理解变化和保护质量的人现在成为瓶颈，那么你有三个选择。 减少生成，找到真正更好的方法来验证或接受较低的质量。

"You are just anti-AI"

每当我批评人工智能时，就会有人说我是卢德主义。 我拒绝适应新世界，坚持旧的方式。

我大量使用人工智能。 这一点我已经说过很多次了。 我每天都使用它，而且我没有兴趣回去手写所有内容。

关键是，我们已经使大规模变更变得极其便宜和快速，而理解这些变更仍然是一项缓慢而困难的工作。 对于变革的作用，我们没有建立正确的心理模型的捷径。

也许有一天我们会找到一个。 截至今天，我认为我们还没有。

你可能是人工智能的重度用户，但仍然认识到它的使用方式存在严重问题。

"More output means more productive"

有人一天产生 10 个 PR，这个数字看起来令人难以置信，这个人的生产力肯定是原来的十倍。

未必。 所谓的 10 倍工程师可能只是窃取周围每个人生产力的人。

如果我一天生成 10 个 PR，但现在三位工程师必须在接下来的两天内审查它们，找出我更改的内容，纠正错误的假设，调试回归并解释为什么需要重做一半，那么我的工作效率并没有提高 10 倍。 我刚刚把工作移交给了其他人。

更糟糕的是，我正在消耗那些通常最难被取代且注意力已经稀缺的人的时间。

PR 数量、更改的行数和“完成”的功能都是糟糕的生产力衡量标准。 您可以让自己的数字看起来令人难以置信，同时降低整个团队的吞吐量。

有些人反驳说，真正的问题是缺乏激励机制的不良组织。 这是真的。 如果你的公司重视票数而不是质量，那么细心的工程师看起来就像是坏员工，而马虎的工程师就会得到晋升。

"Pushing back just makes you're the toxic one"

有人指出，试图控制质量可能会让你被贴上有毒的标签。 其他人都在快速发货，而你是那个说“等等”的人。

我宁愿我的团队中有一个发货量较少但其工作我可以信任的人，而不是一个速度更快的人，他的变化让我想知道我们稍后会发现什么问题。

当业务权衡有意义时，您需要保持灵活性和妥协。 但你还需要一个脊梁。 如果你认为某件事会造成真正的问题，提出来就是工作的一部分。

当生产中断时（确实会发生），我需要进行更改的人真正充分理解它以帮助修复它。 不出现不知道发生了什么。

"Just AI output is like assembly from a compiler"

我们已经相信编译器会生成我们不阅读的机器代码。 为什么这不同呢？

编译器获取代码并将其转换为另一种表示形式，同时保留其语义。 编译器不会决定您的系统应该做什么。 它是确定性的。

法学硕士正在做决定。 它正在选择架构、选择抽象、决定把东西放在哪里。 当你要求 Claude 构建一个功能时，它并没有将你的意图转化为代码。 它正在代表您做出数十个设计决策。

如果五年后我可以给代理一个完整的规范并可靠地验证生成的代码，那么当然，审查代码可能会变得过时，我会很乐意停止这样做。 我们还没有到那一步。

如果您真正理解最终的系统，那就没问题了。 这不是我批评的行为。 但对于绝大多数非常大的 PR，尤其是人工智能生成的 PR，我敢打赌，打开它的人实际上并不理解所有内容。

"We ship 99% AI-generated code and it works"

我也这样做。 我编写的大部分代码都来自人工智能。

你仍然需要付出努力才能理解结果。 如果您正在交付人工智能代码并且您真正了解该系统，那么您就做得对。 这篇文章不是关于你的。

“人工智能可以写代码”≠“我不需要再理解它了”。

你可以大量使用人工智能，但仍然对其产生的结果负责。

"Users don't care. It's just a CRUD app. Ship it and get paid"

我倾向于发现这种观点来自于从事相对较小或孤立项目的人们。

在大型系统中，仅仅让客户满意是不够的。 您需要其他工程师才能理解该系统。 您是否曾经待命并在半夜被叫醒，以修复不是您编写的系统中的生产事件？
